audits.title: P28 Indications for central venous line access for treating infections and the appropriateness of the antimicrobial therapy: a clinical audit
audits.standard: Guidelines for requesting CVAD access and antibiotic selection guidelines

cycle1.result: Good evidence of infection needing IV antibiotics in 49/52; antibiotic selection in line with guidelines in 71.4%, most exceptions discussed with a microbiologist.

audits.other_findings: Poor online documentation meant compliance with CVAD request guidelines could not be confirmed in all cases.
audits.citation: . P28 Indications for central venous line access for treating infections and the appropriateness of the antimicrobial therapy: a clinical audit. JAC Antimicrob Resist. 2022;4(Suppl 1).

audits.title: Maintenance of patency of central venous access devices by registered nurses in an acute ambulatory setting: an evidence utilisation project.
audits.standard: JBI best practice criteria for CVAD flushing
audits.setting: Acute ambulatory cancer setting, National University Health System

cycle1.result: Pulsated flushing 25%; sterile normal saline for flush and lock 68%.

audits.intervention: JBI-PACES and GRiP audit, feedback and re-audit programme (details not reported).
audits.citation: Chong LM, Chow YL, Kong SS, Ang E. Maintenance of patency of central venous access devices by registered nurses in an acute ambulatory setting: an evidence utilisation project. Int J Evid Based Healthc. 2013;11(1):20-25. doi:10.1111/j.1744-1609.2012.00303.x. PMID: 23448326.

audits.title: Road map for improvement: Point prevalence audit and survey of central venous access devices in paediatric acute care.
audits.standard: Basic CVAD care criteria (e.g. dressing clean, dry and intact; site assessment documented)
audits.setting: Six Australian tertiary paediatric hospitals; point prevalence audit

cycle1.result: 13.5% of dressings not clean, dry and intact; 26.4% reinforced with non-sterile dressings; 49.4% had no site assessment documented in previous 4 h; 13.4% had no planned use in next 24 h.

audits.other_findings: Complications in 9.5% of CVADs, mainly blockage (5.7%) and bloodstream infection (1.9%); PICCs had more complications.
audits.citation: Ullman AJ, Cooke M, Kleidon T, Rickard CM. Road map for improvement: Point prevalence audit and survey of central venous access devices in paediatric acute care. J Paediatr Child Health. 2017;53(2):123-130. doi:10.1111/jpc.13347. PMID: 27709723.

audits.title: Reassessing standards of vascular access device care: a follow-up audit.
audits.standard: Evidence-based guidelines for vascular access device care
audits.setting: District general hospital, Princess Royal University Hospital, King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, London

cycle1.result: Poor standards of care and low compliance with evidence-based guidelines.

audits.intervention: Strategy of training, education and standardisation of intravenous devices.

cycle2.result: Standards of care raised and infections reduced (figures not reported).

audits.citation: McGuire R, Norman E, Hayden I. Reassessing standards of vascular access device care: a follow-up audit. Br J Nurs. 2019;28(8):S4-S12. doi:10.12968/bjon.2019.28.8.s4. PMID: 31002548.

audits.title: Using the i-PARIHS theoretical framework to develop evidence implementation strategies for central venous catheter maintenance: a multi-site quality improvement project.
audits.standard: 22 audit criteria from best practice recommendations
audits.setting: Paediatric intensive care units in six tertiary children's hospitals

cycle1.result: Baseline audit against 22 criteria; figures not given in abstract.

audits.intervention: Comprehensive CVC maintenance strategy developed using the i-PARIHS framework.

cycle2.result: 17 of 22 audit criteria showed significant improvement.
